metadata.name: Living Alone

sources.citation: Holt-Lunstad J, Smith TB, Baker M, Harris T, Stephenson D. Loneliness and Social Isolation as Risk Factors for Mortality: A Meta-Analytic Review. Perspect Psychol Sci. 2015;10(2):227-237

metadata.description: Living alone is associated with increased all-cause mortality (OR 1.32, adjusted), comparable to social isolation (1.29) and loneliness (1.26). Participates in the social-category modifier combination rule, so it is attenuated when other social factors are present.
